mainEntity.name: What is Korea crypto PR and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korea crypto PR means securing coverage in Korean-language outlets such as BloomingBit and TokenPost, activating vetted Korean KOLs and KakaoTalk community leads, and building the Korean-language narrative that makes a project credible to Korean retail traders, institutions and exchange listing committees. It is for projects planning a Korean exchange listing, attending Korea Blockchain Week, or building a retail community in Seoul. For the full scope of APAC localisation see the APAC PR service page.

mainEntity.name: How much does Korea crypto PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fractional senior operator running Korea and Japan together typically costs $5K–$12K/month. A full agency with in-country staff will run $15K–$45K/month. KOL activations in Korea are priced separately: nano-tier Korean KOLs run $200–$1.5K per post, micro-tier $500–$5K, and mid-tier $10K–$30K. A Korea-specific launch sprint covering KBW plus two months of follow-on coverage runs $15K–$40K in total.

mainEntity.name: Which Korean outlets and KOLs can you place my project in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Primary Korean crypto outlets: BloomingBit and TokenPost for editorial coverage, plus Hankyung and JoongAng for mainstream crossover when the institutional angle is strong. Korean KOL channels are matched by audience vertical: DeFi, Layer 1, gaming or RWA, with engagement and follower quality checked before any activation. Japan is available in parallel via CryptoTimes JP and CoinPost.

mainEntity.name: How does the Korea PR process work and how long does it take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first two weeks cover the Korean narrative audit and media map. Week three onwards is active outreach to Korean editors and a briefing to the KOL shortlist. First BloomingBit or TokenPost coverage typically lands within four to six weeks if there is a real news hook. KBW timing compresses the window: embargo prep for KBW should start at least eight weeks before the event.
